newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS - CSX, Norfolk Southern set pact to split Conrail.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - CSX, Norfolk Southern set pact to split Conrail.

text.p: CSX Corp. and Norfolk Southern Corp. Tuesday unveiled the highly anticipated details of their proposed $10.3 billion acquisition of Conrail Inc. that call for both railroads to split key routes of the Philadelphia-based carrier.
Under the plan, Norfolk Southern will pay $5.9 billion for 58 percent of Conrail and CSX will pay $4.3 billion for 42 percent of the East Coast railroad.
The plan, outlined in a joint statement, calls for the two railroads to split Conrail's principal routes, giving both key access to the New York-New Jersey region.

"This is really a great moment in the history of rail transportation. What we're seeing is a restructuring of railroading in the eastern portion of the country," Norfolk Southern Chief Executive Officer David Goode said in a telephone interview.
CSX and Norfolk Southern said they will form a jointly-owned entity to acquire all outstanding shares of Conrail for $115 in cash each, or $10.3 billion.

They also said they will file a joint application in June with the Surface Transportation Board, the federal agency that oversees railroad mergers. The railroads said they are hopeful the board will consider the application on an expedited schedule.
"I certainly think this is a transaction they should find very attractive because it does provide competitive rail service to the markets in the Northeast," Goode said.
The pact comes after a five-month bitter fight for control of Conrail, which was formed by Congress in 1976 out of the remains of six bankrupt entities.

Conrail and Richmond, Va.-based CSX announced a friendly merger in October, but the transaction was quickly eclipsed by a hostile and higher bid from Norfolk, Va.-based Norfolk Southern. After a bidding war and a stalemate, CSX last month raised its offer to Norfolk Southern's cash bid of $115 per share and agreed to negotiate a division of assets with Norfolk Southern.

Under the agreement, CSX will operate lines between Boston and Cleveland through Albany and Buffalo, N.Y., with connecting lines into Montreal, New York and New Jersey and between Cleveland and St. Louis.
CSX also will operate Conrail's line connecting New York and Philadelphia and the line that connects Crestline, Ohio and Chicago -- a portion of which is now owned by Norfolk Southern.
Norfolk Southern will operate lines between Chicago and Cleveland and the Conrail line between Cleveland and northern New Jersey via Pittsburgh and Harrisburg, Pa.

In addition, Norfolk Southern will operate the Conrail line serving the metropolitan New York area between northern New Jersey and Buffalo through Binghamton, N.Y., and another between Buffalo and Harrisburg, Pa.

Norfolk Southern also will operate most Conrail lines in Michigan, Maryland, Delaware and Pennsylvania, as well as the routes between Toledo, Ohio, and Detroit, Columbus and Cincinnati, Ohio, and between Columbus and Charleston, W. Va.

The lines that will be taken over by Norfolk Southern are in good condition and well-maintained, Goode said. However, he also said that Norfolk Southern would anticipate making future improvements to meet growing demand for the lines.

The railroads jointly will operate Conrail assets in major terminal areas such as Detroit and northern and southern New Jersey. The two companies also will share access to certain lines in Philadelphia and Indianapolis, and to the rail lines serving the Monongahela coal fields in southwestern Pennsylvania.

The application before the Surface Transportation Board will address traffic flows, terminal operations and related matters; outline the capital investments each company plans to make in new connections and facilities and to increase capacity on critical routes; and detail anticipated savings.
The railroads said implementation of the plan is expected to bring new business and new jobs to the rail industry and the regions now served by both companies.
As part of the agreement, CSX and Norfolk Southern will move to dismiss all pending litigation between the two companies.

CSX's pending tender offer for the remaining shares of Conrail will be amended to include Norfolk Southern and will be extended to May 23. Shares purchased in the offer will be placed in a joint voting trust pending regulatory clearance of the proposed transaction.
The railraods had been expected to announce the asset break-up details in late March, but sources said negotiations in the complicated process took longer than had been expected.
